rationale: Ground truth here is sparse (LGTM approval, four minor style/rebase-scope nits, all resolved in follow-up), and neither candidate hits those specific concerns — both instead dove into deep, largely non-overlapping-with-GT technical bugs (the num_stale_output_tokens double-seed, the Qwen2.5-Omni registry/NamedTuple mismatch, dead async_tokens_to_discard writes), which mutually corroborate and look genuinely grounded. X is more readable and prioritized (Blocking/Should-fix/Minor, concrete fix snippets, an explicit repro and test run), while Y's evidence-quote format is more directly verifiable line-by-line and surfaces one extra plausible finding (NPU randomize_inputs gap) but is denser and harder to action. The two directly contradict each other on the gpu_generation_model_runner randomize_inputs point (X calls it a live bug, Y calls the omission intentional), which caps precision confidence for both. Overall quality and risk are closely matched.
